text: What Holmes tells in the weighing enclosure
why: Holmes has just promised the Colonel that 'you shall know everything' and is leading him to the horse; the label names only that an explanation is coming, without saying what it contains.
Holmes tells the Colonel to 'wash his face and his leg in spirits of wine' in ¶202.
The horse that won 'has not a white hair upon its body' (¶198), and Holmes says washing it will reveal 'the same old Silver Blaze' (¶202), so a disguise is already strongly implied.

text: Race day: in the weighing enclosure, after the race
why: The race has just been run (¶200) and the group has walked into the weighing enclosure (¶202).
